items.definition:
give a right or claim to
This ticket entitles you to free entry.

claim without proof
The police allege that he committed the crime.

to quote as evidence
You must cite your sources in academic writing.

to obtain or get something from
Many English words derive from Latin.

to consider or judge
They deemed the project a success.

be the cause or basis of (something)
The fundamental principles that underlie the theory are complex.

to bury (a corpse)
They decided to inter the remains in the family plot.

to keep; to hold
She managed to retain her composure.

to preoccupy or fill the mind of (someone) continually and to a troubling extent
Don't obsess over small details.

bring to life; give spirit to
The artist used special effects to animate the characters.

to regard something as being caused by
She attributed her success to hard work.

succeed in persuading or influencing (someone) to do something
Nothing could induce him to change his mind.

to make an action or process easy or easier
The new software will facilitate communication between teams.

to kill someone, especially by hanging, without legal trial
Historically, mobs would lynch individuals without trial.

to cause to be or become; to provide
The news rendered him speechless.

to form or devise (a plan or idea) in the mind
She conceived a brilliant plan for the new project.

to declare one's public approval or support of
Many celebrities endorse various products.

to lean or turn away from the vertical or horizontal
The road began to incline steeply uphill.

try to gain the love, support, or custom of (someone)
The company is trying to woo new customers with special offers.

be (a part) of a whole; combine to form (a whole)
These elements constitute the main part of the report.

make full use of and derive benefit from (a resource)
We need to exploit new technologies to improve efficiency.

to make (someone) legally or morally bound to an action or course of action
We were obliged to follow the rules.

to announce officially or publicly
The king will proclaim the new law tomorrow.

see or observe (a thing or person, especially a remarkable or impressive one)
Behold the beauty of the sunset!

to load or burden
The ship was heavily laden with cargo.

officially recognize or authorize
The university is accredited by a national board.

to weaken or damage something (especially a human faculty or function)
Smoking can seriously impair your health.

to forcibly put an end to; to prevent the development or action of
The government tried to suppress the rebellion.

to make consistent or uniform
We need to standardize our procedures.

to relate to; be appropriate to
The rules pertain to all members of the club.

to help or benefit
His efforts did not avail him.

to remove or cleanse
The new leader promised to purge corruption from the government.

to take someone away illegally by force
The police are investigating a case where a child was abducted.

to direct one's hopes or ambitions towards achieving something
She aspires to become a doctor.

to assert something as a position in an argument; to struggle to surmount
The lawyers will contend that their client is innocent.

to hold or express opinions that are at variance with those previously, commonly, or officially expressed
Three judges dissented from the majority decision.

to try hard to do or achieve something
We must endeavor to improve our services.

to bitterly regret (something one has done or allowed to happen)
She would live to rue the day she made that decision.

to eat the evening meal
They would sup together before retiring for the night.

gather or collect (something, especially information or approval)
The politician hoped to garner support from the voters.

put off (an action or event) to a later time; postpone
They decided to defer the decision until next month.

happen or occur afterward or as a result
A heated debate ensued after his controversial statement.

make less severe, serious, or painful
They tried to mitigate the impact of the flood.

make suffering less severe
The new medicine helped to alleviate her pain.

Invent or concoct (something), typically with deceitful intent; construct or manufacture (an industrial product), especially from prepared components.
He tried to fabricate an alibi.

to make something greater by adding to it
He decided to augment his income by working a second job.

have a mutual relationship or connection
Stress levels often correlate with sleep deprivation.

cause severe and disabling damage to
The economic crisis threatened to cripple the industry.

to formally accuse of a crime
The grand jury voted to indict him on fraud charges.

obligate
The contract will obligate them to pay.

reconcile
They tried to reconcile their differences.

remember and honor
A monument was built to commemorate the fallen soldiers.

to make someone a priest or minister; to order by decree
He was ordained as a priest last year.

to assign to a lower position; to banish
The team was relegated to a lower division after losing the match.

to release from a leash or restraint
The dog was unleashed in the park.

to show someone to be involved in a crime or wrongdoing
The evidence seemed to implicate him in the robbery.

to be enough or adequate
A small snack will suffice until dinner.

to surprise greatly
Her incredible performance continued to astound the audience.

To free someone from a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty
The jury decided to acquit the defendant.

ward off (a weapon or attack) with a countermove
He managed to parry the blow with his sword.

be a sign of; indicate
The red light denotes danger.

to harass or oppress, especially for beliefs
Historically, many groups have been persecuted for their religious beliefs.

to match or surpass (a person or achievement), typically by imitation
She tried to emulate her older sister's success.

to surround and have or hold within
The study will encompass all aspects of the problem.
